subject: Prod load test causing elevated 429/5xx across inference endpoints
messages:
From: Sara Kim <sara.kim@velocityhealth.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
Cc: Velocity Health OnCall <oncall@velocityhealth.com>
Date: 2026-09-15T14:05:23Z
Subject: Prod load test: sudden spike in 429/5xx across inference endpoints

Hi Evelyn / Redwood team,

We kicked off our planned velocity-ramp test at 14:00 UTC (staged ramp to ~1200 RPS across regions) and within the first 10 minutes we started seeing a sharp increase in 429 rate and intermittent 5xx (mostly 504/502) from your hosted endpoints. Latency also jumped from median ~80ms to >700ms. Attached are a short sample of error responses and our ramp config (ramp-config.yaml).

This is on our production project (Velocity Health, env=prod); we need immediate help — can you confirm if this is throttling on your side or a misconfiguration on ours? We are pausing further ramp until we hear back.

Attachments: error-sample-429.txt, ramp-config.yaml

Thanks,
Sara
Sara Kim
SRE Lead, Velocity Health
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Kim <sara.kim@velocityhealth.com>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-09-15T14:12:40Z
Subject: Re: Prod load test: sudden spike in 429/5xx across inference endpoints

Thanks Sara — sorry you're seeing this. We're pulling the incident into triage now. Initial asks: could you share the HubSpot deal id (if you want us to tie billing/credits) and the exact model and route you used for the test? I’ve looped in Sean (SRE) and Marcus (infra) to investigate live telemetry.

Immediate plan: 1) collect request traces and sampling of 429/5xx responses; 2) confirm whether rate-limiting/policy triggered; 3) if internal contention, apply temporary routing to a dedicated pool or smaller model. We’ll update within 20–30 minutes.

-Ev
Evelyn Hart
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sara Kim <sara.kim@velocityhealth.com>
Date: 2026-09-15T14:30:05Z
Subject: Re: Prod load test: sudden spike in 429/5xx across inference endpoints

Quick findings from infra:
- At 14:01 UTC we observed a large burst of concurrent requests from Velocity's API keys (~11k concurrency across endpoint shards).
- Autoscaler did not spin up enough warm capacity due to very short ramp windows; backlog and queue growth caused our request admission controller to return 429s (queue full).
- Many 5xx (504) correlate with overloaded downstream model hosts hitting max in-flight requests; some gRPC connections were timing out.
- KV cache eviction rate spiked; prefix cache misses increased token cost and amplified CPU.

Temporary mitigations applied (14:25 UTC):
- Enabled per-key conservative rate-limit and raised admission timeout to avoid cascading retries.
- Deployed an immediate route split to send 25% of traffic to a smaller, cheaper model variant (reduces token work).
- Reduced batch window from 50ms to 25ms for the affected pool to reduce head-of-line latency.

I pulled a trace sample and attached the raw 429 payloads (error-sample-429.txt). Grafana dashboards: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/velocity-ramp (sample link).

Next: recommend formal ramp guidance for Velocity (staged increases + warmup time) and follow-up with a post-incident configuration change: increase warm pool target and add ramp-aware autoscaling policy for production customers doing launches.

-Marcus
Senior SRE, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference
From: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Sara Kim <sara.kim@velocityhealth.com>
Date: 2026-09-15T15:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Prod load test: sudden spike in 429/5xx across inference endpoints

Update from operations: mitigations implemented at 14:25 UTC show an immediate reduction in 429 rate from 18% -> 6% over the next 20 minutes; 5xx rate dropped by ~70%. We also applied a temporary stricter client-side throttling recommendation for Velocity to smooth retries.

Actions taken:
- Routed 25% of traffic to dedicated smaller model pool (works as a graceful degradation path).
- Short-term admission control and reduced batch windows applied.
- Increased the default request timeout to 10s on the gateway to cut unnecessary retries from upstream clients.
- Opened PD incident PD-45123 and notified oncall.

Attached is the CSV of Velocity's ramp requests during the window (velocity-ramp-sep15.csv) for our records. We should schedule a 30-minute sync with Velocity to confirm ramp parameters and provide a ramp guidance doc.

-Sean
SRE Manager
Redwood Inference
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-09-15T15:22:34Z
Subject: Re: Prod load test: sudden spike in 429/5xx across inference endpoints

Looping in for visibility and next steps with the account team. Evelyn — please prep a short executive brief for Velocity's CTO summarizing root cause, immediate mitigations, and our ramp guidance. Sara (cc’d earlier) indicated this is a high-priority production test for their launch. We should also confirm whether a customer credit or SLA exception is necessary — please include suggested credit amount and timeline for a postmortem.

Evelyn, target an Exec Brief and a proposed postmortem timeline (interim update + full RCA within 72 hours). Sean/Marcus, include metrics and action items required to prevent recurrence (ramp-aware autoscale, admission control tuning, recommended client-side backoff).

-Lauren
VP, Customer Success
Redwood Inference
From: Sara Kim <sara.kim@velocityhealth.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-09-15T16:00:12Z
Subject: Re: Prod load test: sudden spike in 429/5xx across inference endpoints

Thanks for the quick response and mitigations — we see overall error rates dropping and appreciate the split routing. Two asks from our side: 1) can you provide explicit ramp guidance (RPS per minute per region + warm-up time) so we can re-run the test safely; 2) we’d like an immediate 30-minute sync today to walk through the mitigations and your recommended launch plan.

We paused the next stage of the ramp for now. We’ll accept a 30-minute call this afternoon (any time after 16:30 UTC).

Best,
Sara
